model: Holdco look-through sum-of-the-parts NAV: proportionate Loblaw and Choice Properties equity cash flows capitalised at cost of equity (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: GWL 52.6% look-through share of PC Financial sale consideration (~C$800M to Loblaw, EQB shares + cash, closed 2026-07-01)
equity_bridge.note: PC Financial is discontinued in FY2025 and excluded from the stream; its sale proceeds are a balance-sheet item not in the flows. 0.526 x 800. Analysis JSON cites ~C$1.3bn total value/excess capital released; the headline consideration is used, conservatively.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (consolidated, ~ Loblaw sales growth), trimmed for the 53rd week in FY2025
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-8% 5y) diverges >30% from revenue and EPS and is meaningless for this holdco: GWL's attributable book equity shrinks because it buys back ~C$1bn/yr of its own stock and records changes in subsidiary ownership through equity. Reported EPS is distorted by fair-value swings on the Choice Trust Unit liability and Exchangeable Units (FY2024 C$-399M, FY2025 C$-11M); adjusted diluted EPS grew 12.1% to C$4.46 in FY2025. NAV/share (market-price basis) compounded 22.6%/yr 2022-2025 on Loblaw's re-rating.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on consolidated OCF - capex (pre-lease, pre-interest, pre-NCI) and say little about GWL's own claim; the forward stream is rebuilt on a look-through basis instead. SBC adjustment not applicable (expensed inside the adjusted earnings basis).

scenario_narratives.base: Loblaw executes its 2026 guide: ~4% sales growth as ~75 mostly hard-discount stores open each year, earnings outgrowing sales on private label, PC Optimum retail media and pharmacy-services mix, while the C$10bn 2026-2030 capex plan holds owner-FCF conversion near 70% before it normalises to 85%. Choice Properties delivers 2-3% same-asset NOI and FFO/unit of C$1.08-1.10. GWL keeps its stake percentages flat by selling into Loblaw's NCIB and pays ~C$140M/yr of corporate cost and cash tax on those disposals. The holdco discount is an observation about price, not a cash flow; it is not charged in the value beyond that corporate leakage.
scenario_narratives.bull: The discount-format land grab works: No Frills/Maxi maturation and pharmacy scope-of-practice expansion lift look-through sales growth toward 5% and the earnings margin to ~5.7%, PC Optimum data monetisation scales, and once the network build is done reinvestment needs fall (88% conversion). Choice Properties' First Capital deal (with KingSett) is accretive and lifts NAV growth. GWL's own NCIB, including Wittington participation, keeps shrinking the share count at a discount to NAV, which is accretive per share.
scenario_narratives.bear: Political and competitive pressure caps grocery margins: a federal grocery code of conduct with teeth or price-control rhetoric, Costco/Walmart/Metro matching on price, and hard-discount stores cannibalising conventional banners leave the look-through earnings margin drifting down to 4.7%. Sales growth slows to ~2-3% in a weak Canadian consumer environment, the capex plan earns near its cost of capital (80% terminal conversion), and higher Canadian rates widen Choice Properties' cap rates. The bread price-fixing legacy produces further civil claims (Metro/Sobeys).

valuation_philosophy.summary: George Weston is valued as what it is: a holding company whose shareholders own 52.6% of Loblaw's and ~61.7% of Choice Properties' equity cash flows, less a holdco cost and leakage layer and GWL Corporate's own debt and preferred shares. The C$64.5bn of consolidated revenue is a consolidation artifact. MARKET SOTP (management's NAV method, live prices at inputs.price_as_of, 2025-12-31 holdings): Loblaw 618.7M sh x C$62.64 = C$38,755M + Choice Properties 446.4M units x C$14.77 = C$6,593M - GWL Corporate debt 498 - preferred shares 835 + cash 301 (= -1,032) = C$44,317M / 379.5M shares = C$116.78 NAV/share (company's own FY2025-end figure: C$115.86). The stock at the current price trades ~13% below that market NAV (18% at FY2025-end). INTRINSIC SOTP (this model): instead of trusting the subsidiaries' share prices, the proportionate equity cash flows of both are capitalised at a 7.5% CAD cost of equity: FY0 look-through adjusted earnings C$1,668M (Loblaw 1,437 + Choice 446 - consolidation 76 - corporate 140) on C$33,852M of proportionate revenue, converted to owner FCF at 70% during the 2026-2030 capex plan and 85% terminal, less GWL Corporate net debt and prefs (C$1,032M), plus GWL's share of PC Financial sale proceeds (C$421M). The two NAVs answer different questions: the market NAV says how wide the holdco discount is; the intrinsic NAV says whether the underlying Loblaw/Choice prices are themselves justified. Loblaw at ~26x adjusted earnings is priced richly; the intrinsic look-through value comes in BELOW the market NAV, so most of the observed 'holdco discount' is the market declining to pay Loblaw's own multiple twice, plus the capitalised corporate drag (~C$140M/yr is ~C$2.5bn, ~C$6.5/share at 7.5%/2% growth), rather than a free mispricing.
key_risks_to_valuation: Look-through conversion of earnings to owner FCF (70% -> 85%) is an estimate: Loblaw's standalone FCF is not in the extracted GWL filings, and every 5pp of terminal conversion is worth roughly C$4-5/share.
The stream is valued at one cost of equity for a blend of grocery (~85% of value) and REIT equity (~15%); Choice Properties would merit a similar rate given its 7.0x Debt/EBITDAFV leverage.
Holdings vintage: stakes, corporate net debt and GWL share count are all 2025-12-31; 2026 interims are not extracted. Mutually consistent, but a re-anchor to Q3-2026 is needed.
Capital-gains tax on GWL's NCIB participation (low tax basis in Loblaw) is a permanent leakage; if GWL sold larger blocks the tax drag would rise.
Grocery affordability politics: a code of conduct with pricing teeth or windfall-tax rhetoric hits ~85% of the value at once.
Controlled company (Wittington ~59%): no takeover or activist path to close the discount; the only lever is the buyback.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (WN.TO regular close; L.TO and CHP-UN.TO closes at the same timestamp for the market SOTP); 52-week range 83.18-107.94.
data_sources.financials: GWL FY2025 Annual Report (research/WN.TO/Extracted/WN.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt): segment highlights and adjusted net earnings contribution table (lines ~1110-1330), GWL Corporate free cash flow (lines 557-576), Net Asset Value table (lines 2310-2375), Loblaw NCIB participation (line ~1611), Outlook (line 4508). Metrics.csv for consolidated history (post-split share basis).

inputs.sbc_source: Not deducted separately: Loblaw and Choice Properties SBC is already expensed inside the adjusted net earnings the look-through stream is built from, and GWL's own small SBC sits inside the GWL Corporate cost drag. Adding a separate SBC line would charge it twice; house and street bases therefore coincide (band collapses).
inputs.share_count_basis: 379.5M common shares outstanding at 2025-12-31 (FY2025 AR NAV table, post 3-for-1 split of 2025-08-18) plus ~1.0M dilutive options = 380.5M. Held flat: GWL's buybacks (C$993M in FY2025) are funded from the look-through flows already counted, so letting the count fall too would double-count them. All history in Metrics.csv is on the post-split basis (FY2016 384.1M = 128M x 3).
inputs.base_revenue_basis: GWL's PROPORTIONATE look-through revenue, not consolidated revenue: 52.6% x Loblaw FY2025 revenue C$63,903M scaled to 52 weeks (x52/53, FY2025 had a 53rd week) + 61.7% x Choice Properties revenue C$1,415M = C$33,852M. Loblaw stake = 618.7M of ~1,176M shares; Choice = 446.4M units held directly (Trust + Class B LP).
inputs.margin_basis: ebitda_margin_path carries the look-through ADJUSTED NET EARNINGS margin (already after subsidiary interest, leases, SBC and tax), so D&A, tax and SBC paths are zero by construction. FY0: Loblaw contribution 1,465 x 52/53 = 1,437 + Choice Properties 446 - consolidation effect 77 x 52/53 = 76 - GWL Corporate non-financing cash drag 140 (admin ~40 + cash tax on NCIB-participation gains ~100; FY2025 corporate cash tax 119, FY2024 142) = C$1,668M, 4.93% of proportionate revenue. Pref dividends and GWL debenture interest are NOT in the stream; the prefs and debt are in net_debt instead (charged once).
inputs.capex_basis: capex_pct_path is the reinvestment drag: the share of look-through earnings retained for growth (Loblaw net growth capex above maintenance D&A, ~C$2.4bn gross 2026 guide vs ~C$1.75bn non-lease D&A, and Choice Properties development/maintenance above FFO). Owner-FCF conversion of earnings runs 70% in the 2026-2030 C$10bn store/DC plan, rising to 85% terminal (2.5% terminal growth at a ~15-17% RONIC, Loblaw's adjusted ROC is 15.2%). FY0 owner FCF = 1,668 x 0.68 = C$1,134M (last_fcf).
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: reported_fcf is the company-defined GWL Corporate free cash flow C$1,208M FY2025 (dividends from Loblaw 426 + Choice distributions 343 + Loblaw NCIB proceeds 906 - corporate/financing costs 348 incl. one-off C$247M bread-settlement provision payment - tax 119). It is not reconcilable to last_fcf by the SBC/interest formula: last_fcf is the look-through owner FCF; the cash GWL actually receives exceeds it because Loblaw distributes more than its FCF (dividends + buybacks ~C$2.6bn vs FCF ~C$2.0bn) and levers up to do it.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, CAD: Government of Canada 10y ~3.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~0.75 (defensive grocery/pharmacy + grocery-anchored REIT, plus a small premium for controlled-company governance and NCIB-tax leakage) = ~7.0%, rounded up to 7.5%. Equity rate because the stream is post-subsidiary-interest; subsidiary debt is NOT deducted again. Same rate in every scenario (risk charged once in the scenarios).
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases are inside the stream: Loblaw adjusted net earnings are after IFRS-16 ROU depreciation and lease interest (~lease cash cost, C$1,031M net lease payments FY2025). Lease liabilities (C$6.4bn) are therefore NOT in net_debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only: the stream is GWL's proportionate share (52.6% Loblaw, 446.4M CHP units); no NCI deduction in the bridge. Consolidated revenue/EBITDA/debt in Metrics.csv are a consolidation artifact and are not used as the base.
inputs.notes: MODEL: George Weston is a pure holding company (52.6% of Loblaw, 446.4M Choice Properties units, a small GWL Corporate layer). Routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md: holdco straddling the operating-company and REIT rows -> value the parts separately and sum. An owner-FCF DCF on the C$64.5bn consolidated financials is rejected: ~47% of Loblaw and ~38% of Choice belong to minorities, consolidated debt (C$24.6bn incl. leases) is non-recourse to GWL, and GWL's own claim is a proportionate share of each subsidiary's equity cash flow. Implementation: the proportionate post-interest equity flows of both subsidiaries (one look-through stream) are capitalised at a cost of equity through the engine, less GWL Corporate's own debt + preferred shares net of cash (C$1,032M at 2025-12-31, exactly the deduction in the company's NAV table), plus GWL's share of the PC Financial sale proceeds. This is the intrinsic counterpart to management's market-price NAV (Loblaw shares x L.TO price + CHP units x CHP.UN price - corporate net debt and prefs), which is reported alongside in valuation_philosophy. Balance-sheet vintage: FY2025 annual is the latest extracted filing (2026 interims not in Extracted/); stake counts, corporate net debt and GWL share count are all the same 2025-12-31 snapshot, which keeps them mutually consistent (GWL sells Loblaw shares into the NCIB and uses the proceeds to buy back its own shares, which moves numerator and denominator together). Refresh all four from the Q3-2026 report when extracted.
inputs.price_note: Regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

bear.capex_rationale: Conversion 68/68/70/72/74/76/78/80/80/80%: new hard-discount stores cannibalise the conventional banners and the capex plan earns close to its cost of capital.

base.growth_rationale: Loblaw 2026 guide: retail earnings grow faster than sales, adjusted EPS high single digits, ~75 new (mostly hard-discount) stores; proportionate sales ~4% decaying to 2.5% as the 2026-2030 capex plan matures. Choice same-asset NOI +2-3%.
base.margin_rationale: Look-through earnings margin 4.93% FY0 rising ~1.5%/yr relative (earnings ahead of sales) to 5.36% by year 9: discount-store maturation, PC Optimum retail media, pharmacy services.

bull.capex_rationale: Conversion 70/71/73/76/79/82/85/87/88/88%: the discount build-out earns well above the cost of capital and reinvestment needs fall once it is done.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20%, above the 15% default: the main risk is a single regulator/political axis (grocery affordability scrutiny) that can cap margins across the whole stake, not solvency, since GWL Corporate carries only C$0.5bn of debt and C$0.8bn of prefs. Base 55% because Loblaw has a long record of meeting guidance in a non-discretionary category. Bull 25%, below the 35% default, because it needs both the discount build-out to earn well above its cost of capital AND structurally lower reinvestment afterwards.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
